answer: Agents mapping umber soil on a mesa must lock $100 per active identity for 30 days. The market checks the escrow at each scheduling pulse and caps each funded identity at one job per round. Creating 1,000 sybils therefore requires $100,000 locked up for a month, plus transaction fees; splitting one deposit across aliases adds no capacity. This makes identity multiplication cost scarce capital and the returns that capital could otherwise earn.
